name: Mozilla Common Voice
description: Mozilla Common Voice is a massive, publicly available multilingual dataset of human voices designed to train speech applications. It relies on worldwide volunteer contributors who read sentences aloud and validate recordings made by others across over 100 languages, making speech technology accessible in low-resource languages.

license.name: Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal
license.notes: Audio clips and text sentences are dedicated to the public domain under Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0-1.0). Downloading and using dataset releases requires agreeing to the Mozilla Common Voice Terms of Use, which strictly prohibit attempting to determine the identity of speakers or re-identifying contributors.

source_references.title: Mozilla Common Voice Terms of Use
source_references.notes: Specifies acceptable use policy and strictly forbids speaker identification and deanonymization.

source_references.title: Common Voice: A Massively-Multilingual Speech Corpus
source_references.notes: Published in LREC 2020 by Rosana Ardila et al.

verification.notes: Metadata verified against official Mozilla Common Voice platform, Terms of Use, and LREC 2020 paper.

citation.paper_title: Common Voice: A Massively-Multilingual Speech Corpus

provenance.collection_method: Crowdsourced through web and mobile browsers where volunteers read public domain sentences into their microphones.
provenance.curation_notes: Each audio clip must be upvoted by at least two distinct peer reviewers to be marked as validated. Re-identifying individual speakers or deanonymizing contributors is strictly prohibited by Mozilla's platform terms of use.
